## Prime-Agent System Prompt (ACP Template)

For file editing operations, the prime-agent runtime exposes a pre-installed `mcp` Python object with `list_tools` and `call_tool` methods. Use them to discover and invoke tools.

Example discovery and call:

```python
tools_list = await mcp.list_tools("tools")
for t in tools_list:
    print(t["name"], t["inputSchema"])

result = await mcp.call_tool("tools", "ox-bridge-write", {"path": "/tmp/x.py", "content": "# code here"})
print(result)
```

The `tools` MCP server exposes:
- `ox-bridge-write`: write a file (args: `path`, `content`)
- `ox-bridge-edit`: edit a file with hunks (args: `path`, `edits` = [{old, new}])
- `ox-bridge-read`: read a file region (args: `path`, `start`, `end`)

All bridging calls return synchronously. Print results to confirm before proceeding.

Everything is green. Here's the refactor:

**`/workspace/core.mjs`** — pure core, zero `fs`/`process`/`console`:
- `wordFrequencies(text) → Map<string, number>` — lowercases, splits on `[^a-z']+` (so apostrophes survive: `don't`)
- `formatTop(counts, topN) → string` — sorts by count desc, ties alphabetical asc, emits `"count\tword\n"` lines (empty string for empty input)

**`/workspace/cli.mjs`** — thin shell:
- `main({ argv, env, out })` with defaults pulled from `process` at call time, not import time — so tests can inject all three
- Reads the file, pipes through the core, writes to the provided stream
- The bare `run()` is gone; execution only happens via an `import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href` entrypoint check, so importing the module has no side effects

**`/workspace/wordfreq.test.mjs`** — 9 tests via `node --test`, all passing:
- Case folding (`The the THE → the: 3`)
- Apostrophes kept (`Don't stop, don't ever stop → don't: 2`)
- Empty/punctuation-only text
- Tie-breaking verified exactly: count desc then alpha asc
- topN larger than vocabulary, and topN truncation
- One integration test spawning `node cli.mjs sample.txt` with `TOP_N=3` in a temp dir fixture, asserting exact stdout `"3\tworry\n2\tdon't\n2\tstop\n"`
